1 of 5. Meera, your accounts lead, pulls a shortlist of customers who spent over ₹5,000. Along the way the system also works out each customer's total spent and discount. She then uses the shortlist to ask 'which orders belong to these customers?' She never said which detail to use for matching. What should happen?
  A) Match on the customer's ID alone and ignore the extra worked-out details. The check just works.  B) Stop and tell her she must say which detail to match on before it will run.  C) Match on the first extra detail the system happened to work out, such as total spent.
  Your answer (a letter, or your own words) >

2 of 5. Ravi asks for 'phone numbers only' of customers who spent over ₹5,000. Behind the scenes the system has also worked out total spent and a discount figure. What should his list show?
  A) Only the phone numbers he asked for. The extra figures stay out of the list.  B) Phone numbers plus the total spent, because it was used to pick the customers.  C) Phone numbers plus every extra figure, so staff can see how each customer was picked.
  Your answer (a letter, or your own words) >

3 of 5. Sunil asks for customer name AND phone number together, but then uses that list to check 'is this order from one of these customers?', which only works with one detail per customer. What should happen?
  A) Stop with a clear message that one detail per customer is needed. Do not guess.  B) Quietly use the first detail (the name) and carry on.  C) Carry on with the first detail, but show a warning that the other was ignored.
  Your answer (a letter, or your own words) >

4 of 5. The fix is for the 'is this customer among these?' check. Your team also uses other checks: 'exactly matches this one customer', 'does any order exist for this customer?' and 'combine two customer lists'. Should the fix change those too?
  A) Fix only the 'is among these' check. Leave the others as they are, and add tests showing they still work.  B) Apply the same fix to all of these checks at once.  C) Fix only the 'is among these' check now, and bring in the others later after a separate review.
  Your answer (a letter, or your own words) >

5 of 5. Your team has reports that already work fine, with worked-out figures and no helper figures, used in 'is among these' checks. Should the fix change anything for them?
  A) No. Their results and behaviour stay exactly as today.  B) Update them to the new tidier behaviour, even if a few results differ slightly.  C) Keep them as is, but flag any report whose results would now differ so a manager can review.
